answer: A stake-bonded identity registry resists Sybils by making each agent lock a refundable deposit before it can trade. Like a quartz crystal that only grows under pressure, reputation accrues slowly through verified work, while a whisper network of peer attestations flags clusters of fresh accounts acting in lockstep. Misbehavior triggers slashing, so an attacker faces a ferrous, unyielding cost: every fake identity burns real capital, and mass-producing agents becomes more expensive than any profit the fraud could yield.
